target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and any-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that (1) heading checks block valid headingless skills, (2) any-line overlap is trivially bypassable — a plan document sharing a single heading or boilerplate line receives `requiresExplicitApproval=false` and overwrites the skill, and (3) zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser, rejects empty bodies, and uses a **substantial-continuity classifier** that requires at least 3 shared non-heading body lines AND at least 50% of original non-heading content retained before allowing automatic apply. Low-continuity updates force pending approval even under `auto` policy, preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites while blocking incidental-overlap plans that share only headings or 1-2 boilerplate lines.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Low-continuity update proposals (insufficient shared content with current SKILL.md) are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Substantially continuous updates (≥3 shared non-heading lines, ≥50% original content retained) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid headingless skill updates apply normally when they retain substantial content
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The low-continuity approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for low-continuity updates while substantially continuous updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`**

**Live approval-hook proof (terminal transcript from exact head)**:

The `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` function is the approval hook that determines whether an agent-initiated `apply` action proceeds automatically or requires operator approval. Under `auto` policy, it returns `undefined` (no approval required) for actions that pass all checks. For low-continuity updates, it returns `requireApproval` with a warning prompt, which blocks the agent from applying the proposal until the operator approves. SKILL.md remains unchanged until approval is granted.

```console
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T10:15:40.062Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Low-continuity update blocked by approval hook (auto policy) ---
SKILL.md before proposal:
  ---
  name: weather
  description: Weather skill
  ---
  
  # Weather
  
  Steps to check weather.
  Check the forecast.
  Save the result.

Approval hook result: requireApproval (BLOCKED)
  title: "Apply workspace skill proposal"
  severity: "warning"
  allowedDecisions: ["allow-once","deny"]
SKILL.md unchanged after approval hook block: true

--- Proof 2: Incidental heading-only overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 3: Incidental 1-line overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 4: Incidental 2-line overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 5: Substantial continuity update allowed (auto policy) ---
Approval hook result: undefined (ALLOWED)

--- Proof 6: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged after rejection: true

=== Summary ===
1. Low-continuity update: approval hook returns requireApproval, SKILL.md unchanged ✅
2. Heading-only overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
3. 1-line overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
```

**Substantial-continuity classifier detail** (exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`):

Related: #95838

## What Problem This Solves

PR #95838 added the additive `heartbeat_outcomes` table but also advanced the per-agent SQLite schema marker from 11 to 12. That contradicted the deliberate version-11 consolidation and made a short-lived unreleased build rewrite existing v11 databases to v12.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat table uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, and the agent database owner executes the canonical schema on every open. It therefore fits the existing structure-gated version-11 schema without a new version marker.

This change folds the heartbeat table into the documented v11 surface and adds a regression test that starts from an existing v11 database without that table. Reopening creates the table while both `PRAGMA user_version` and `schema_meta.schema_version` remain 11.

The short-lived v12 marker was never shipped in a release. Any local database already opened by that main-only build should be backed up and have its two version markers corrected manually; steady-state runtime does not gain a downgrade shim.

## User Impact

Current-main operators remain on per-agent schema version 11 while retaining bounded heartbeat outcome storage. No table, column, or persisted heartbeat data is removed.

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): guard provider catalog live URL parsing against malformed responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchLiveProviderModelRows` / `fetchLiveProviderModelIds` would crash with an uncaught `TypeError` when a provider model catalog API returns a genuinely malformed absolute URL in its `next` / `links.next` pagination field, or when the guarded fetch reports an unparseable redirect target (`finalUrl`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveLiveModelCatalogNextPage` and `fetchLiveProviderModelRows` each called `new URL()` on external API response data without try/catch. The fix introduces a `tryParseUrl` helper that returns `undefined` on parse failures, matching the defensive pattern already used by `withoutMatrixStateAfterSyncParam` in the Matrix transport (#109759).

When a provider-advertised next URL is malformed or cross-origin, the fix attempts cursor-based pagination as a fallback, then returns the controlled `incomplete` result when no fallback remains — preventing silent catalog truncation.

## User Impact

Provider live model discovery survives misbehaving catalog APIs without crashing; a malformed pagination URL surfaces a controlled incomplete-pagination error instead of an uncaught TypeError or a silently truncated catalog.

## Evidence

**Before (upstream main — TypeError crash through real guarded fetch):**

```json
{"ok":false,"error":"TypeError: Invalid URL","label":"before-fix"}
```

**After (this branch — controlled incomplete-pagination error through real guarded fetch):**

```json
{"ok":false,"error":"Error: proof model discovery did not include a supported next page before the catalog completed","label":"after-fix"}
```

The harness drives the real exported `fetchLiveProviderModelIds` through a loopback HTTP server using the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` and `ssrfPolicyFromHttpBaseUrlAllowedHostname`. The malformed `next` URL contains a space in the hostname (`http://exa mple.com/p2`), which is a genuinely invalid absolute URL that triggers the native `new URL()` parse failure.

**Focused tests (24 passed):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

New tests cover: malformed absolute `next` URL (incomplete-pagination error), malformed nested `links.next` URL, cursor fallback recovery from malformed URL, unparseable `finalUrl` (cross-origin replay header fallback), and malformed `next` with `has_more: true`.

**What was not tested:** Live provider catalog APIs returning malformed pagination URLs; the loopback harness proves the defensive parsing guard on the real exported function through the production guarded-HTTP stack.

target.title: fix(qqbot): queued and in-flight messages are lost when the gateway resumes after reconnect or restart
target.body:
Closes #109996

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users' messages would silently vanish — no reply, no error — whenever the gateway connection dropped, the server requested a reconnect, or the gateway process restarted while their message was still queued or being processed.

The QQ gateway replays only events with `seq` greater than the RESUME seq, but the channel committed (and persisted to the SQLite session store) each frame's seq at receipt, before the queued handler ran. Any message in flight or in the in-memory per-peer queue at disconnect/restart time was skipped by the resume replay and permanently lost. Handler failures had the same outcome: the message was logged-and-dropped locally while the already-advanced seq defeated the protocol's replay. This is the same defect family as the ClickClack reconnect-cursor race fixed in #108577, with the added severity that the premature cursor is persisted across process restarts (5-minute resume window).

## Why This Change Was Made

Message-frame seqs now commit to the RESUME watermark only when the message settles. A new `SeqWatermark` tracks in-flight message seqs: the resumable value stays just below the oldest unsettled message, so RESUME replays anything still queued, in flight, or failed; frames without queued work (READY, RESUMED, interactions, acks) commit immediately, exactly as before. Settling means the handler completed, or the message was intentionally discarded (queue-full eviction, urgent queue clear) — intentional drops settle so the watermark cannot wedge behind a message the channel chose to discard. Handler failures do not settle, matching the ClickClack fix and the Telegram bot-update-tracker safe-watermark semantics: reconnect redelivers the message instead of losing it. The previously fire-and-forget message dispatch also gets a rejection handler so routing failures are logged and left pending for replay.

Delivery semantics move from at-most-once (silent loss) to at-least-once across reconnects: a crash after a handler completes but before the throttled session save can redeliver an already-handled message. That matches the durable-before-ack convention used by the Telegram/WhatsApp/Slack/Signal channels.

## User Impact

QQ Bot messages received while an agent turn is running — or queued behind one — now survive reconnects, server-driven RECONNECTs, and gateway restarts within the resume window: the gateway replays them and the bot answers. Previously they disappeared with no trace. No config, protocol, or persisted-state shape changes.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real GatewayConnection, real `ws` client, protocol-compatible local gateway)

Driver: the production `GatewayConnection` (real websocket client, real reconnect/backoff, real event dispatcher and per-peer message queue) connected to a local WebSocket server implementing the QQ gateway protocol: HELLO → IDENTIFY → READY(s=1), and RESUME → replay events with `seq > resume seq`. A message event `s=2` is delivered while its handler is still running, then the server drops the socket.

Before (current `main`) — the client resumes at the already-committed seq and the message is lost:

```
[server] IDENTIFY received — sending READY (s=1)
[proof] delivering message event seq=2 (handler will hang in flight)
[client] handler invoked for m-inflight (call #1)
[server] dropping the client connection (transient network failure)
[client] WebSocket closed: 1006
[server] RESUME received with seq=2 — replaying 0 event(s) with seq>2
[proof] FINAL: resumeSeq=2 handledAfterReplay=(none)
```

After (this patch) — the client resumes below the unprocessed message, the server replays it, and it is handled:

```
[server] RESUME received with seq=1 — replaying 1 event(s) with seq>1
[client] handler invoked for m-inflight (call #2)
[client] handler COMPLETED for m-inflight
[proof] FINAL: resumeSeq=1 handledAfterReplay=m-inflight
```

### Regression coverage

- `seq-watermark.test.ts` (new): commit/register/settle semantics, out-of-order settles, replay boundary, session reset.
- `gateway-connection.test.ts` (4 new integration tests): message seq is not committed until the handler completes; reconnect RESUME asks for replay below an unprocessed message; failed handlers hold the watermark; queue-full eviction settles so the watermark cannot wedge.
- Against unfixed `main`, all 4 new integration tests fail (RESUME seq advances past the in-flight message); the 7 pre-existing disconnect-status tests pass unchanged in both states.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on `seq-watermark.test.ts` + `gateway-connection.test.ts` + `message-queue.test.ts` → 26 passed.
- Pre-existing `outbound-dispatch.test.ts` failures on this machine reproduce identically without this change (unrelated outbound media-path surface).
- Scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass on the five changed files.

### Sibling-surface context

The receive-path audit that found this also checked the other channels for the same premature-cursor family: Telegram's default isolated ingress advances its offset only after durable spooling, WhatsApp journals inbound before ack, Slack and Signal are durable-before-ack, and iMessage clamps its catchup cursor below failed rows — qqbot was the remaining gateway-resume surface committing before processing.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseWithLimit()` in video/music generation provider download paths capped `maxBytes` but omitted `chunkTimeoutMs`. A server that accepts the connection and then stops sending body chunks can leave the download Promise pending indefinitely, exhausting the Gateway connection pool under concurrent video downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` on every video/music download path that was missing them, matching `google/video-generation-provider.ts` and `anthropic/usage.ts`. Resolve `ProviderOperationTimeoutMs` (`number | () => number`) to a concrete number before passing it to `chunkTimeoutMs` so TypeScript and the idle timer see a finite budget. Add a caller-path OpenAI regression that feeds a never-chunking `ReadableStream` body and asserts the production download error within the request deadline.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled upstream video/music download body could hang the provider download forever.

**After:** Download body reads fail closed after the operation idle budget with a clear `…download stalled: no data received for Nms` error, releasing the connection.

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs` via `resolveOpenAIVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/byteplus/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveBytePlusVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveRunwayVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/together/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveTogetherVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/fal/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/openrouter/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: params.timeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: resolveMinimaxRequestTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` (both URL and file_id paths) |
| `extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/provider-http-mocks.ts` | Wire `createProviderOperationTimeoutResolver` + `resolveProviderOperationTimeoutMs` to honor explicit `deadline.timeoutMs` |
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts` | Add `stalledVideoResponse()` fixture + caller-path regression |

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled generated-video download bodies now fail closed on the shared reader idle budget instead of hanging the download forever.

### Canonical reachability path

`generateVideo` → `downloadOpenAIVideo` → `readResponseWithLimit(response, maxBytes, { chunkTimeoutMs, onIdleTimeout })` (`extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts:270`); sibling providers wire the same option bag into their download reads.

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `video/mp4` headers plus one body chunk and then never sends another chunk or ends the response (post-header download stall). The production shared reader (`readResponseWithLimit` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` — the exact runtime the download path imports) is driven against that live socket with the provider's `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` option bag, Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server sends video/mp4 headers + one chunk then stalls; drive the
# production download reader against it (idle budget 300ms):
```

target.title: fix(anthropic): complete transcript reverse-scan windows across short reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a Claude session transcript in the session catalog can fail with a
`Claude transcript changed while it was being read` error even when the file was
not touched.

`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts`
scans the transcript backwards in fixed windows. Each window was filled with a
single positional `handle.read(chunk, 0, size, position)` that then required
`bytesRead === size`, throwing otherwise. A positional read is allowed to return
fewer bytes than requested, so a benign short read tripped that check and failed
the transcript page with a message implying the file changed. The window is
in-bounds (`position` starts at `requestedEnd ≤ stat.size` and only decrements,
`size = min(chunk, position, …)`), so a short read there is not on its own a
reason to fail the page. The forward metadata scan in the same function already
completes short reads by looping; only this reverse scan threw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reverse scan now fills each window across as many reads as it takes,
advancing both the buffer offset and the file position each read, so a benign
short read no longer surfaces a "transcript changed" error. A zero-byte read
before the window is filled is premature EOF, so that case still throws the same
error — only benign positive short reads stop failing the page. This is the same
loop the forward scan in this file already uses, and it follows the recently
merged short-read completion work (#108941, #108655, #108253) that had not
reached this plugin path; it is a different surface from #108242, which fills
bounded windows in the core gateway (`src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts`).

## User Impact

Paging a Claude session transcript no longer fails with a spurious "Claude
transcript changed while it was being read" error when a benign positive short
read occurs in the reverse-window scan. A zero-byte read before the window is
filled (premature EOF, consistent with the file being truncated or replaced
mid-read) still surfaces the same error.

## Evidence

Changed files: `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts` (reverse-scan fill
loop) and `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (two regression tests).

The two colocated unit tests lock the regression behavior: one drives
`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` through capped short positional reads and asserts
the paged items/order/cursor match a normal read across two pages; the other
forces a zero-byte read mid-window and asserts the existing premature-EOF error
still raises.

Real-behavior proof came from driving the **exported** `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage`
against a real on-disk, secretless Claude JSONL transcript of 204929 bytes (larger
than the 128 KiB reverse window) while capping the underlying `FileHandle.read` to
4096 bytes — the same real transcript and capping logic run against the
current-main module (before) and this branch (after). Raw run:

```text
real readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage · real FileHandle.read · transcript 204929 B · read cap 4096 B
baseline (before) SHA e0478e2d · after (this PR) SHA 223e79bca3

[1] NORMAL CONTROL   (after,  uncapped)  3 real reads · page-hash c573fe29… (2 pages)
[2] SHORT READ       (before, cap 4096)  throws "Claude transcript changed while it was being read" at read #1
[3] SHORT READ       (after,  cap 4096)  82 real reads · page-hash c573fe29… · identical to [1]: true
[4] ZERO-BYTE EOF    (after)             throws "Claude transcript changed while it was being read"
```

The `page-hash` is over both pages' items, ordering, and `nextCursor`; case [3]
matching case [1] means identical pagination. Of the 82 reads in [3], 79 are
within-window contiguous fills (buffer offset and file position each advance by
the previous read's length); the remaining reads are the first read of each new,
lower reverse window (position steps down), across the two requested pages.

Reproduce: on each SHA, call the exported `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` against
a >128 KiB Claude JSONL transcript while capping the underlying `FileHandle.read`
to 4 KiB; before the fix the first capped read throws, after the fix the windows
are completed and the two-page items/ordering/cursors are identical to an
uncapped read.

Focused suite: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` — 27 passed (25 existing + 2 new);
before the fix: 1 failed | 26 passed. oxfmt and oxlint clean; extensions
typecheck reports no errors in the changed files.

target.title: feat(macos): honor the selected microphone in Talk and show live voice activity in chat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Talk Mode on macOS records from the system-default microphone regardless of the input device the user selected in Voice settings, offers no echo cancellation or gain control, and the chat surface gives no feedback while talking — no level meter, no visible listening state, and no transcript. The web chat shows live voice activity and honors the configured input device.

## Why This Change Was Made

Round 2 of aligning the native macOS chat with the web chat (follow-up to #109712), scoped to the talk-input ownership area:

- Talk now binds its `AVAudioEngine` capture to the microphone selected in Voice settings (`voiceWakeMicID` stays the single authoritative selection, shared with Voice Wake); empty selection keeps the system default.
- Voice processing (echo cancellation/AGC) is enabled when the device supports it, with a one-retry fallback to a plain engine when a device rejects it.
- Device unplug/default changes mid-talk restart capture safely (observer-driven); the saved selection is retried on the next start. A Core Audio edge is guarded where `AVAudioEngine.inputNode` can abort without a usable default device.
- `TalkModeController` now publishes smoothed level, phase, partial transcript, and the last 20 final utterances; the chat composer renders a live waveform on the talk button, a Listening/Thinking/Speaking status, and an expandable rolling transcript strip.
- Right-clicking the talk button lists available input devices (plus System Default) and patches the same authoritative setting.
- Shared `OpenClawChatTalkControl` gains additive, defaulted fields (level, transcripts, devices, selection callback) — iOS keeps compiling unchanged and can adopt later.

## User Impact

Talking to OpenClaw from the native chat now uses the microphone you chose, sounds cleaner on supported devices, survives device changes, and shows what the app hears while you speak — matching the web chat's feedback. The menu-bar talk overlay is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --target OpenClawChatUI` and `swift build --package-path apps/macos --configuration release` — pass (re-verified after rebase onto landed main).
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --parallel` — 864 tests pass.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel` — 1309 pass; new suites: device-selection resolution (6 tests), controller publishing (2), talk-activity views (4).
- `pnpm lint:swift`, `pnpm format:swift`, `pnpm native:i18n:sync` (inventory committed; translations to follow in the i18n pass) — clean.
- Structured review: one reported compile-error finding was rejected as false — the flagged OSLog concatenation pattern is pre-existing in the same file on main (TalkModeRuntime.swift:533-548) and the tree passed two independent release builds.
- Live microphone capture requires interactive permission and was not exercised end-to-end; control rendering and all decision logic are unit-tested.

target.title: fix(signal): drain accepted inbound events on stop
target.body:
## Summary
- Keep Signal durable-ingress debounce entries marked as accepted until their first flush or cancel completes.
- Force accepted debounced Signal entries to flush when the monitor aborts, while retaining abort cancellation for reply-session conflict retry backoff.
- Keep the Signal ingress drain alive until already-started monitor tasks finish so adoption can tombstone accepted claims before teardown.

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Chore

## Scope
- [ ] Gateway
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] Auth
- [ ] Memory
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API
- [ ] UI/UX
- [ ] CI
- [x] Signal plugin

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where Signal users could lose an inbound message that signal-cli had already accepted when the monitor stopped before the configured inbound debounce timer fired.

Closes #103881

## Why This Change Was Made
Signal now tracks durable-ingress-owned debounce entries separately from inline enqueue work, and monitor abort forces those accepted debounce keys through their first flush. Retry waits after a reply-session initialization conflict still observe the monitor abort signal and cancel instead of continuing stale retries.

## User Impact
Signal messages accepted just before shutdown or reconnect teardown are delivered once instead of being skipped by the initial debounce abort check. Shutdown still avoids unowned delayed work and still cancels retry backoff after the first accepted attempt.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A Signal inbound event accepted before monitor shutdown completes its initial debounced flush instead of being skipped when the monitor aborts.
**Environment tested:** Linux, Node v24.16.0, pnpm v11.2.2, local source checkout.
**Steps run after the patch:** Ran the Signal monitor regression test that accepts a debounced inbound event, aborts the monitor before the debounce window elapses, and asserts the reply is delivered once; also ran the reply-session retry cancellation and durable ingress lifecycle suites.
**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.pairs-uuid-only-senders-uuid-allowlist-entry.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.reply-session-conflict.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.sends-tool-summaries-responseprefix.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ingress-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/signal/src/signal-ingress.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-signal.config.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  61 passed (61)
   Duration  30.41s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 36.19s
```

**Observed result:** The buffered accepted-before-stop Signal monitor test now observes one reply delivery; the retry-conflict suite still confirms pending retry backoff is canceled after monitor stop.
**Not tested:** Live signal-cli daemon/SSE traffic against a real Signal account.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: Signal only treated entries as shutdown-drainable while `enqueue()` was actively awaited. Timer-backed debounce work had already returned from `enqueue()`, so monitor abort could reach the initial flush before dispatch and skip an accepted durable event.
- Missing guardrail: The existing stop coverage only proved inline accepted work drained and retry backoff canceled; it did not cover a durable, debounced event accepted before stop but flushed after abort.

## Regression Test Plan
- Updated the Signal monitor stop regression to cover a buffered inbound message accepted before stop.
- Re-ran the issue's focused monitor tool-result shard plus durable ingress and reply-session conflict retry suites.

## Impact Assessment
- Scope: Signal monitor/event handler only; no config, schema, or public API surface changes.
- Downstream: Normal Signal debounce entries with durable ingress lifecycle are affected; control-lane immediate commands and unowned delayed work keep their existing behavior.
- Edge cases: Covers abort before the timer fires and abort racing immediately after enqueue returns.
- Hard-coded values: None introduced.

## Security Impact
- New permissions? No
- Secrets handling changed? No
- New network calls? No

## Verification
- `pnpm format extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.pairs-uuid-only-senders-uuid-allowlist-entry.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.pairs-uuid-only-senders-uuid-allowlist-entry.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.pairs-uuid-only-senders-uuid-allowlist-entry.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.reply-session-conflict.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.sends-tool-summaries-responseprefix.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ingress-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/signal/src/signal-ingress.test.ts` passed: 5 files, 61 tests.

target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`newSession()` and `resumeSession()` in the ACP bridge send the `session_info_update` notification via `sendSessionSnapshotUpdate` BEFORE returning the JSON-RPC result. Clients that key off `session_info_update` to learn the sessionId receive a notification referencing a sessionId they have not yet parsed from the result.

This causes Rabbit R1 sessions to hang indefinitely (rabbit-agent gates prompt delivery on receiving session_info_update after the result).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix defers the notification and subsequent `sendAvailableCommands` to fire asynchronously after the result is returned, using `setTimeout(..., 0)` to cross the response-write boundary. Both `newSession()` (line 394) and `resumeSession()` (line 554) are fixed. The full promise chain has a terminal `.catch()` handler.

## User Impact

Clients that expect session_info_update after the session/new or resume result now receive correct ordering. No change to the API contract, response shape, or notification content.

## Evidence

### Ordering tests (transport-level)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```
Two new tests verify that `session_info_update` is NOT called before the lifecycle handler resolves, and IS called after flushing timers — confirming result-before-notification ordering at the transport boundary.

### All ACP tests
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

### Typecheck
```
pnpm tsgo:core — EXIT: 0
```

### Fix pattern
Before: `await sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...)` → `return { sessionId, ... }`
After:  `return { sessionId, ... }` → `setTimeout(() => sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...).then(...).catch(...), 0)`

target.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws export <agent-id> --out <new-directory>`
- project one installed agent into the grouped portable Claw schema
- copy ledger-managed workspace files and safe workspace-relative avatars into package sidecars
- always assign regenerated exports a derivative package identity and content-derived version
- omit nonportable remote avatars, normalize empty optional arrays, and expand `~` in output paths

## Scope

Export reads the provenance established by the add/status lifecycle and writes a new self-contained package without mutating the installed Claw. It accepts an exact agent id, explicitly projects portable agent fields, copies only ledger-managed workspace files plus a validated local avatar, emits exact recorded package references, and refuses unavailable managed files or an existing output directory.

Image data avatars remain inline. A safe local avatar is read through the pinned workspace avatar boundary, copied under `workspace/`, and rewritten to a workspace-relative manifest path. Remote, missing, or unsafe local avatars are omitted because they are not portable package state.

Every regenerated package is emitted as `openclaw-claw-<agent-id>@0.0.0-export.<content-hash>`, including an unchanged installation. Export never reuses an authenticated publisher's package name/version unless it can return the byte-for-byte original artifact, which this command intentionally does not do.

This slice emits the schema's JSON-compatible representation. The later dedicated #106888 slice changes the canonical exported representation to `CLAW.md` while preserving this package and round-trip behavior.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102296 status/remove and ownership-aware lifecycle state
- This PR: portable creation/export experience
- Next: #102383 gateway-owned cron lifecycle
- Canonical `CLAW.md`: #106888

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across all 6 PR files
- Oxfmt: all 6 PR files correctly formatted
- 8 export unit tests
- 15 Claws CLI tests
- 8 full lifecycle E2E tests
- `git diff --check`
- Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

The real CLI E2E passes consent-bound add preview/apply -> export -> inspect -> consent-bound add preview/apply from the exported package in isolated state. Export writes `package.json`, `openclaw.claw.json`, managed workspace sidecars, and a portable agent manifest; the fresh add recreates the agent from the derivative package.

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. No user facing changes.

4.37.1 - 16 Jul 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml.   • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

target.body:
Closes #104545

## What Problem This Solves

When `models.mode: "replace"` filters the model catalog, the Control UI showed the resulting models without explaining why other bundled or discovered models might be absent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured model-list responses now carry additive `catalogMode: "replace"` metadata. The chat model picker and Quick Settings use that metadata to explain that model settings are filtering the catalog, without claiming that every visible row was explicitly configured. Full-catalog (`view: "all"`) responses do not carry the hint metadata.

The picker action opens the Models section directly at `/settings/ai-agents?section=models#config-section-models`.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

Cyber:

```text
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

target.title: fix(sandbox): cancel CDP probe response bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sandbox browser startup could leave HTTP response streams open after CDP readiness probes. Both unsuccessful probes that continued the retry loop and successful probes that returned early left unread response bodies for garbage collection, which could retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForSandboxCdp` now cancels every probe response body before branching on the HTTP status. Successful probes, retry timing, auth headers, and startup timeout behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox browser auto-start keeps the same readiness and failure semantics, while each completed CDP probe promptly releases its connection instead of leaving an unread stream open.

## Evidence

**Real-machine before / premise / after / negative control**

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.5.0.

I ran the same production-function harness from an `upstream/main` snapshot and this branch. The harness starts a real localhost `node:http` server, sends a streaming HTTP response through real Node fetch, calls the production `waitForSandboxCdp` loop, and observes the server-side TCP socket 250 ms after the function returns:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-before 200
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-after 200
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-after 503
```

The harness loads the probe loop from `src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts` (mirrored in `/tmp/sandbox-cdp-probe-*.ts` for import isolation). The server never ends its response body, making socket closure a direct observation of consumer cancellation rather than normal body completion.

Negative control / before (`upstream/main` at `e01027dd28a`), streaming HTTP 200:

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":200,"cdpReachable":true,"serverObservedSocketClose":false}
```

After (`aac0533a40b`), streaming HTTP 200 and 503:

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":200,"cdpReachable":true,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":503,"cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
```

The unchanged `cdpReachable` values are the behavioral controls: successful probes still succeed and unsuccessful probes still fail, while the real server observes prompt connection release in both paths.

Premise: Undici 8.5.0, installed by this repository, documents that every response body must be consumed or canceled because Node garbage collection does not release connection resources promptly. This probe only needs the response status, so cancellation is the bounded cleanup operation.

Focused validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts -t "CDP probe response body"
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       4 passed | 46 skipped (50)

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
exit 0

git diff --check
exit 0
```

Full build and broader suites were not run locally; fork GitHub Actions cover the wider gates. This is a non-visual transport cleanup, so no screenshot is applicable.

target.title: fix(e2e): share ClawHub preflight timeout across fetch and body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Crabline inbound injection and runtime-parity mock `/debug/requests` fetches could hang indefinitely. Both paths used `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without `timeoutMs` and then called bare `response.json()`, so a hung or never-finishing admin/mock endpoint could stall the suite forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copy the existing `suite-runtime-gateway` pattern: pass `timeoutMs: 15_000` into `fetchWithSsrFGuard` and read JSON through `readProviderJsonResponse` on both surfaces. Add a caller-path hang regression for runtime-parity capture and a focused Crabline inbound assertion that the production helper receives the timeout + bounded JSON reader.

## User Impact

No end-user product change. QA Lab / Crabline CI scenarios fail closed on hung inbound or mock debug endpoints instead of hanging the suite process.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-inbound-bounds.test.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts`
- Production caller paths:
  - `postCrablineInbound` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` + `readProviderJsonResponse`
  - `captureRuntimeParityCell` → `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` → same pattern

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

QA Lab Crabline inbound injection now fails closed on a hung/stalled admin-inbound endpoint instead of hanging the scenario forever, and completing bodies still parse through the bounded reader.

### Canonical reachability path

`postCrablineInbound` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ url: adminInboundUrl, timeoutMs: QA_LAB_CRABLINE_INBOUND_TIMEOUT_MS })` → `readProviderJsonResponse` (`extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts:202`).

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` admin-inbound server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `200` headers plus one JSON chunk (`{"update":`) and then never sends another chunk or ends the response. The production helper `qaLabCrablineInboundTesting.postCrablineInbound` (exported via `extensions/qa-lab/api.ts`) is driven against that live socket with a minimal adapter manifest pointing at the server (`policy: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }` allows loopback), Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP admin-inbound server returns headers + one chunk then stalls; drive
# the production postCrablineInbound helper against it:
node --import tsx scripts/proof-qa-lab-crabline-inbound.mts

# Supplemental focused regressions:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-inbound-bounds.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts --reporter=dot
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production Crabline inbound helper against a live socket):

```text
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 15000ms (elapsed 15001ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:54050/stall
  ok: stalled inbound rejected (not hung) — elapsed=15046ms
  ok: bounded by the configured guarded-fetch deadline — elapsed=15046ms, budget=15000ms
  ok: unbounded inbound json() still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing inbound parsed message id — 42

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled admin-inbound socket, `postCrablineInbound` fails closed at ~15046ms — exactly the configured `QA_LAB_CRABLINE_INBOUND_TIMEOUT_MS` guarded-fetch deadline (`[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 15000ms`) — instead of hanging. The negative control — a raw `response.json()` on the same stalled socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing body still parses to the telegram message id via the bounded reader.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real Crabline admin-inbound or mock `/debug/requests` endpoint outside the harness.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the guarded-fetch timeout + bounded JSON wiring and caller-path proof output.

target.title: fix(ui): Realtime Talk hangs when Google Live connections stall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI users starting Realtime Talk with Google Live could remain stuck in the connecting state when the browser WebSocket never opened or opened without Google ever completing protocol setup. During that stall, the microphone, camera stream, input meter, and both audio contexts could remain active indefinitely. A socket error or close before readiness could leave the same resources active until the user manually dismissed the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser WebSocket construction has no caller-configurable startup deadline, so the Google Live transport now owns a 30-second deadline covering the full startup phase through the current socket's Google `setupComplete` frame. This matches the existing Realtime Talk WebRTC setup deadline while using the provider-specific readiness signal instead of treating the lower-level WebSocket `open` event as ready.

Timeout, error, and close paths report the transport error and stop the current socket lifecycle exactly once. Captured-socket checks before and after asynchronous message decoding keep stale socket events from clearing a replacement attempt's timer or emitting readiness for it. The conflict resolution with the merged Gemini Live video work preserves camera-frame shutdown, media-track release, and `onVideoStream(null)` cleanup.

## User Impact

Google Live Realtime Talk now fails with a clear error instead of connecting forever when either the WebSocket handshake or Google protocol setup stalls. Failed, closed, and timed-out attempts release the microphone, camera, input meter, socket, and both AudioContext instances without waiting for another user action.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3614ee6fa9287672c58763ffeecb048819a59f9c`, based on `8020dd3e0830ead01dc81c8a446444078315b63d`. The branch was rebuilt from current `main` using only the two substantive PR commits, removing two historical merge commits and resolving the sole conflict with #109719's video lifecycle.

- Regression coverage proves both pre-open and post-open/no-`setupComplete` timeout paths. The video-enabled path verifies audio and camera tracks stop, the socket closes, and `onVideoStream` receives `null` after the combined stream.

target.title: fix(msteams): bound remote media saves with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote media downloads had **no body-read idle timeout** on any code path. If a QQ CDN host returned response headers successfully but then stalled mid-body (network congestion, server-side hang, TCP keep-alive without data), the download would hang indefinitely.

Three affected code paths on `main` before this fix:

| # | File | Path | Issue |
|---|------|------|-------|
| 1 | `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts` | `downloadFile()` → `fetchMedia()` | Passed `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000` but omitted `readIdleTimeoutMs` |
| 2 | `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts` | `fetchMedia()` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer()` | Forwarded `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` but dropped `readIdleTimeoutMs` from the pass-through |
| 3 | `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts` | `downloadFile()` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer()` | Passed no timeouts at all — only `{ url, filePathHint }` |

In `src/media/fetch.ts`, `responseBodyChunks()` only guards the read when `readIdleTimeoutMs` is present; otherwise it falls through to `await reader.read()` with no timeout, so a stalled body blocks forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000` (plus the existing `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000`) through all three QQBot media paths and the `FetchMediaOptions` pass-through, matching the timeout policy already used by Mattermost, Zalo, and Tlon media fetches.

## User Impact

**Before:** A QQ CDN host that returned headers then stalled mid-body could hang a QQBot media download forever.

**After:** Stalled media bodies fail closed after the 30s idle budget with a clear `Media download stalled: no data received for Nms` error, releasing the connection.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts`, `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts`, `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts` (+ tests)
- Production caller path: QQBot `downloadFile` / `fetchMedia` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ readIdleTimeoutMs })` → `readResponseWithLimit(..., { chunkTimeoutMs })`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

QQBot media downloads now idle-timeout a stalled response body instead of hanging forever.

### Canonical reachability path

QQBot `downloadFile` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ url, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })` → `readResponseWithLimit(res, maxBytes, { chunkTimeoutMs })` (`src/media/fetch.ts:643`).

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that sends `image/png` headers plus one body chunk and then never sends another chunk or ends the response. The production `readRemoteMediaBuffer` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-runtime` — the exact function the QQBot fix passes `readIdleTimeoutMs` into) is driven against that live socket, following the repo's own `fetch.test.ts` real-transport pattern (public-looking `lookupFn` so the SSRF guard passes, `fetchImpl` connecting to the local server). Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server sends media headers + one chunk then stalls; drive the
# production media reader against it (idle budget 300ms):
node --import tsx scripts/proof-qqbot-media-idle-timeout.mts

# Supplemental focused regressions:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts --reporter=dot
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production media reader against a live socket):

```text
  ok: stalled media read rejected (not hung) — elapsed=496ms
  ok: media read terminated (bounded, not infinite) — elapsed=496ms
  ok: failure surfaced as MediaFetchError — Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:52599/stall: Media download stalled: no data received for 300ms
  ok: unbounded media body read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing media body read intact — bytes=7

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled `image/png` socket, `readRemoteMediaBuffer` fails closed in ~496ms with `Media download stalled: no data received for 300ms` and releases the connection. The negative control — an unbounded `arrayBuffer()` on the same socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing body still reads intact.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real QQ CDN endpoint.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the QQBot media timeout pass-through and caller-path proof output.

target.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating a cron job with `--system-event` (main session job), the `--channel` and `--to` options are silently discarded. Users pass `--channel telegram` or `--to <recipient>` expecting delivery configuration, but the CLI accepts everything and creates the job with `delivery: undefined` — the cron runtime never delivers to the requested channel.

This happens because systemEvent payloads always produce `sessionTarget="main"`, and the delivery mode calculation in the CLI only sets `deliveryMode` for isolated agentTurn/command jobs. The `--channel` default value (`"last"`) is fine to pass through, but an explicitly-set `--channel` or `--to` should be rejected with a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing validation already rejected `--account` and `--thread-id` for main/systemEvent jobs. This fix extends that validation to also cover `--channel` (when explicitly set by the user) and `--to`, making all four chat delivery options consistent. The same guard was added to `cron edit` so both entry points enforce the same resulting-job delivery invariant.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw cron add --name test --every 1h --system-event wakeup --channel telegram` → CLI validation passes silently, job is created with no delivery
- **After**: same command → clear error: `--channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.`
- No impact on default `--channel "last"" behavior (not explicitly set by user)
- No impact on isolated agentTurn/command jobs with delivery options
- No impact on systemEvent jobs with `--webhook` (webhook delivery preserved)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof: before/after CLI transcript

**Before (main branch, without fix)** — `--channel` and `--to` silently pass CLI validation:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "before-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)
# GatewayTransportError: gateway closed ... (Gateway not running, unrelated)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "before-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)
EXIT: 1
```

**After (fix branch)** — `--channel` and `--to` are rejected with clear error:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-webhook" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --webhook "https://example.com/hook"
# CLI validation passed (webhook delivery preserved for systemEvent jobs)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-nochannel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup"
# CLI validation passed (default channel="last" is not explicitly set)
EXIT: 1
```

### Regression tests

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.test.ts` — 9 tests covering rejected/allowed delivery-option combinations for cron add.
- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.test.ts` — 8 new tests covering the same guard on cron edit, including existing-job resolution.

### Root cause traced

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts` — the guard only checked `accountId || hasThreadId`, but `hasChatDeliveryTarget` already included `optionSource("channel") === "cli"` and `typeof opts.to === "string"`. The fix extends the guard to include all four conditions.
- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.ts` — applies the same guard to edits, resolving the resulting job from existing state when the final session target or payload kind is ambiguous.
- `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts` — `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` returns `{mode:"none"}` for any job that is not isolated+agentTurn/command
- `src/cron/service/jobs.ts` — `assertDeliverySupport` explicitly rejects channel delivery config for non-isolated session targets

### Revision notes

target.title: fix: prevent connection retention on guarded redirect failures

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where guarded HTTP redirects could leave an unread response body attached to the dispatcher when the redirect was rejected because of a missing or invalid `Location`, a loop, or the redirect limit. Repeated failures could delay connection reuse and retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancel and await every redirect response body before validating the next hop, while preserving the existing redirect, authorization, and dispatcher cleanup behavior. Cancellation failures remain non-fatal.

## User Impact

Guarded fetch callers now cleanly release redirect responses on all rejection paths, improving reliability under repeated malformed or looping redirects without changing accepted redirect behavior.

target.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

New users finish onboarding with a bare install even when their Mac is full of apps
OpenClaw already has plugins and skills for (Notion, Obsidian, Slack, 1Password,
Things, …). Nothing connects "what is installed on this machine" with "what OpenClaw
can do with it", so discovery is manual catalog browsing.

# Why This Change Was Made

Adds installed-app plugin/skill recommendations to `openclaw onboard`:

1. **Scan** — enumerate `/Applications`, `~/Applications`, and a small allowlist of
   `/System/Applications` (TCC-free: no permission dialog can fire — `readdir`,
   Launch Services, and Spotlight metadata are unprotected paths; verified on a real
   machine).
2. **Candidates** — loose name matches from the official plugin/channel/provider
   catalogs plus top-3 ClawHub skill search hits per app (concurrency 4, 5s/request,
   20s overall budget; failures degrade to catalog-only candidates).
3. **AI matching** — one completion on the model route the wizard just verified. The
   model receives app names + candidate descriptions and returns genuine matches with
   a tier (`recommended`/`optional`) and a short reason. No curated bundle-id map to
   maintain; the model rejects coincidental name overlaps (naive matching paired
   Linear→`line`, Zed→`zededa`, Parallels→`parallel` in prototyping — the live test
   asserts these traps stay dead).
4. **Consent surface** — the wizard step is deliberately "magical" (product decision):
   no consent prompt before the scan, but the scanning progress line and the results
   note both disclose that app names are matched using the configured model and
   ClawHub search, and `wizard.appRecommendations: false` disables the feature
   entirely. The results step lists detected apps and installs only what the user
   selects (recommended tier pre-checked, explicit skip).
5. **Remote gateway path** — the TS node-host gains the `device.apps` invoke command
   Android already ships (same envelope; macOS emits `label`/`bundleId` where Android
   emits `label`/`packageName`). Node-side sharing is **off by default** (privacy
   parity with Android's consent toggle) via node-host config /
   `--share-installed-apps`; disabled invokes return the typed
   `INSTALLED_APPS_SHARING_DISABLED` error. The gateway allowlists the command for
   macOS nodes and strips it everywhere when the kill switch is off. Local onboarding
   scans directly and does not use the node command.

Also fixes a latent bug this feature exposed: `runSetupInferenceTest` applied the
32-token verification-probe output cap (`SETUP_INFERENCE_TEST_MAX_TOKENS`) to every
completion, so any custom prompt longer than a few words returned a reasoning-only
turn and "Agent couldn't generate a response." Custom-prompt completions now use the
model's own output budget; the probe keeps its cap.

Prior art: Setapp is the only mainstream product doing install-scan → recommendation;
its trust framing (scan silently, show the detected list, act opt-in) is what this
follows, with explicit disclosure because app names do leave the machine.

# User Impact

- `openclaw onboard` (non-quickstart, macOS, working model route) gains one optional
  step: detected apps → tiered multiselect → install. Zero matches or any failure
  (offline ClawHub, model error, malformed model output) skips the step silently;
  onboarding never blocks on this feature.
- New config key `wizard.appRecommendations` (default enabled) to disable.
- Mac/headless nodes can opt in to sharing their app inventory with the gateway
  (`--share-installed-apps`, persisted in node-host config, default off).

# Evidence

- **Live end-to-end test** (real ClawHub `/api/v1/search` + real OpenAI
  `gpt-5.6-luna`): `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENAI_API_KEY=… pnpm test:live
  src/system-agent/setup-app-recommendations.live.test.ts` — **passed** (76s). Fixture
  inventory of 9 real apps incl. traps; model matched Notion→`notion`,
  Obsidian→`obsidian`, Slack→`slack-api`, Linear→`linear`, Things→`things-mac`,
  1Password→`1password` and produced none of the trap pairings.
- **Unit tests** (all passing): scanner fixtures/filtering/sorting + Linux-safe plist
  reader injection; candidate dedupe + ClawHub failure degradation; matcher zod
  filtering incl. fenced-JSON/extra-key/overlong-reason tolerance; node `device.apps`
  gating + Android-parity envelope; gateway allowlist + kill-switch stripping;
  node-host config persistence; wizard gating/pre-check/skip/install paths
  (`pnpm test src/infra/installed-apps.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-app-recommendations.test.ts
  src/node-host/invoke-device-apps.test.ts src/node-host/runtime.test.ts
  src/node-host/config.test.ts src/wizard/setup.app-recommendations.test.ts
  src/gateway/node-command-policy.test.ts src/wizard/setup.test.ts
  src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts`).
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `git diff --check` —
  all green.
- Autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): two accepted findings fixed (Linux CI
  plutil dependency in the scanner test; unbounded ClawHub phase → 20s budget). The
  remaining consent-first finding is consciously rejected as the documented product
  decision (default-on with disclosure + kill switch); an inline comment records it.
- Real-machine scan prototype: 45/52 apps matched, no TCC prompt, <2s.

target.title: fix(utils): preserve JSON parse error context in JSON5 fallback path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback()` silently discards the `JSON.parse` error when both `JSON.parse` and `JSON5.parse` fail. Callers currently lose the stricter JSON diagnostic context and only receive the JSON5 error. This preserves both errors with the JSON5 diagnostic as the backward-compatible top-level message and the strict JSON error attached as `cause`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function now catches both errors explicitly, preserves the JSON5 diagnostic as the top-level error message (backward compatible ??existing callers checking only `.message` still see the JSON5 line-and-column info), and attaches the strict JSON.parse error as `Error.cause` for callers that need it. The fast path (strict JSON succeeds) and JSON5 fallback (single parser fails) are unchanged.

## User Impact

Callers can extract both the JSON5 diagnostic (from `.message`) and the strict JSON error (from `.cause`), enabling better debugging without breaking backward compatibility or exposing raw input in default log output.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/utils/parse-json-compat.test.ts --run` ??passed. Existing unit tests for the strict JSON path and JSON5 fallback path continue to pass; the dual-failure path now preserves JSON5 in `.message` with strict JSON error as `.cause`.

- Controlled runtime proof: standalone function proof with Node.js. `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback("not valid")` now throws `Error("JSON5 fallback also failed: ...", { cause: SyntaxError("Unexpected token...") })`. Callers checking `.message` see the same JSON5 diagnostic as current main; callers needing strict JSON detail can inspect `.cause`.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete parse-json-compat test suite was also attempted: all tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases were skipped. The affected focused regression is green.

target.title: fix(anthropic): complete transcript reverse-scan windows across short reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a Claude session transcript in the session catalog can fail with a
`Claude transcript changed while it was being read` error even when the file was
not touched.

`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts`
scans the transcript backwards in fixed windows. Each window was filled with a
single positional `handle.read(chunk, 0, size, position)` that then required
`bytesRead === size`, throwing otherwise. A positional read is allowed to return
fewer bytes than requested, so a benign short read tripped that check and failed
the transcript page with a message implying the file changed. The window is
in-bounds (`position` starts at `requestedEnd ≤ stat.size` and only decrements,
`size = min(chunk, position, …)`), so a short read there is not on its own a
reason to fail the page. The forward metadata scan in the same function already
completes short reads by looping; only this reverse scan threw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reverse scan now fills each window across as many reads as it takes,
advancing both the buffer offset and the file position each read, so a benign
short read no longer surfaces a "transcript changed" error. A zero-byte read
before the window is filled is premature EOF, so that case still throws the same
error — only benign positive short reads stop failing the page. This is the same
loop the forward scan in this file already uses, and it follows the recently
merged short-read completion work (#108941, #108655, #108253) that had not
reached this plugin path; it is a different surface from #108242, which fills
bounded windows in the core gateway (`src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts`).

## User Impact

Paging a Claude session transcript no longer fails with a spurious "Claude
transcript changed while it was being read" error when a benign positive short
read occurs in the reverse-window scan. A zero-byte read before the window is
filled (premature EOF, consistent with the file being truncated or replaced
mid-read) still surfaces the same error.

## Evidence

Changed files: `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts` (reverse-scan fill
loop) and `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (two regression tests).

The two colocated unit tests lock the regression behavior: one drives
`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` through capped short positional reads and asserts
the paged items/order/cursor match a normal read across two pages; the other
forces a zero-byte read mid-window and asserts the existing premature-EOF error
still raises.

Real-behavior proof came from driving the **exported** `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage`
against a real on-disk, secretless Claude JSONL transcript of 204929 bytes (larger
than the 128 KiB reverse window) while capping the underlying `FileHandle.read` to
4096 bytes — the same real transcript and capping logic run against the
current-main module (before) and this branch (after). Raw run:

```text
real readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage · real FileHandle.read · transcript 204929 B · read cap 4096 B
baseline (before) SHA e0478e2d · after (this PR) SHA 223e79bca3

[1] NORMAL CONTROL   (after,  uncapped)  3 real reads · page-hash c573fe29… (2 pages)
[2] SHORT READ       (before, cap 4096)  throws "Claude transcript changed while it was being read" at read #1
[3] SHORT READ       (after,  cap 4096)  82 real reads · page-hash c573fe29… · identical to [1]: true
[4] ZERO-BYTE EOF    (after)             throws "Claude transcript changed while it was being read"
```

The `page-hash` is over both pages' items, ordering, and `nextCursor`; case [3]
matching case [1] means identical pagination. Of the 82 reads in [3], 79 are
within-window contiguous fills (buffer offset and file position each advance by
the previous read's length); the remaining reads are the first read of each new,
lower reverse window (position steps down), across the two requested pages.

Reproduce: on each SHA, call the exported `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` against
a >128 KiB Claude JSONL transcript while capping the underlying `FileHandle.read`
to 4 KiB; before the fix the first capped read throws, after the fix the windows
are completed and the two-page items/ordering/cursors are identical to an
uncapped read.

Focused suite: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` — 27 passed (25 existing + 2 new);
before the fix: 1 failed | 26 passed. oxfmt and oxlint clean; extensions
typecheck reports no errors in the changed files.

target.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws export <agent-id> --out <new-directory>`
- project one installed agent into the grouped portable Claw schema
- copy ledger-managed workspace files and safe workspace-relative avatars into package sidecars
- always assign regenerated exports a derivative package identity and content-derived version
- omit nonportable remote avatars, normalize empty optional arrays, and expand `~` in output paths

## Scope

Export reads the provenance established by the add/status lifecycle and writes a new self-contained package without mutating the installed Claw. It accepts an exact agent id, explicitly projects portable agent fields, copies only ledger-managed workspace files plus a validated local avatar, emits exact recorded package references, and refuses unavailable managed files or an existing output directory.

Image data avatars remain inline. A safe local avatar is read through the pinned workspace avatar boundary, copied under `workspace/`, and rewritten to a workspace-relative manifest path. Remote, missing, or unsafe local avatars are omitted because they are not portable package state.

Every regenerated package is emitted as `openclaw-claw-<agent-id>@0.0.0-export.<content-hash>`, including an unchanged installation. Export never reuses an authenticated publisher's package name/version unless it can return the byte-for-byte original artifact, which this command intentionally does not do.

This slice emits the schema's JSON-compatible representation. The later dedicated #106888 slice changes the canonical exported representation to `CLAW.md` while preserving this package and round-trip behavior.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102296 status/remove and ownership-aware lifecycle state
